title: No tax on overtime? Only the half counts
label: Tax myth vs fact

hook.sub: The new deduction isn't what you think.

beats.text: Check your *overtime premium* on your pay stubs.
beats.sub: It's a deduction, so it still shows as wages.

cta.sub: We'll DM you our year-end tax checklist.

captions.instagram:
"No tax on overtime" doesn't cover all of your overtime pay.

✔️ Only the premium counts: the extra half in time-and-a-half. At $30/hour regular and $45 overtime, $15 per hour is deductible.
✔️ Cap: $12,500 a year single, $25,000 married filing jointly, for 2025 to 2028.
✔️ It phases out above $150,000 of income ($300,000 joint). You don't have to itemize.
✔️ It's a deduction on your return, so your paycheck still shows the overtime as wages.

Source: IRS, Working Families Tax Cuts.
